summary: The Knuth-Morris-Pratt algorithm finds a pattern inside a text in O(n + m) time. It preprocesses the pattern into a failure table so that, after a mismatch, it never re-examines text characters that are already known to match.

sections.heading: The problem with naive search
sections.body: Naive matching slides the pattern one position at a time and restarts comparison from the pattern's start, costing O(n·m) in the worst case (for example text 'aaaaaaab', pattern 'aaab').

sections.heading: The LPS (failure) array
sections.body: lps[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix of pattern[0..i] that is also a suffix of it. It tells KMP how far the pattern can safely fall back after a mismatch at position i + 1. For 'aabaaac' the table is [0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 2, 0]; for 'AAAA' it is [0, 1, 2, 3].

sections.heading: Matching
sections.body: Walk the text with i and the pattern with j. On a match advance both. On a mismatch, if j > 0 set j = lps[j - 1] (reuse the matched prefix), otherwise advance i. When j reaches m, the pattern occurs at i - m.

sections.heading: Complexity
bullets: Search: O(n); i never moves backward and each fallback strictly decreases j, bounded by the advances.
Total O(n + m) time, O(m) extra space.

sections.body: LPS for the pattern: [0,0,1,2,0,1,2,3,4]. Matching reaches ABAB then mismatches at D versus C; j falls back to lps[3] = 2, keeping 'AB' matched, and continues without moving i backward, finally matching at index 10.
Instead of stopping at j == m, record i - m and set j = lps[m - 1] to allow overlapping matches, then keep scanning.
Compare a hash of each text window with the pattern's hash, updating the window hash in O(1) and verifying on a match. Average O(n + m), worst O(nm), and easy to extend to multiple patterns.

The Z-function gives similar guarantees with simpler code. Boyer-Moore compares from the pattern's end and can skip many characters, making it fastest in practice on long patterns and natural-language text.

bullets: Finding periodic structure: the smallest period of a string is m - lps[m-1] when it divides m.

takeaways: KMP avoids re-comparing text by using the pattern's own prefix-suffix structure.
lps[i] = longest proper prefix of p[0..i] that is also a suffix.
O(n + m) time and O(m) space.
Compare with Rabin-Karp and Boyer-Moore for other trade-offs.

references.label: Knuth, Morris, Pratt: Fast Pattern Matching in Strings (1977)
